scenario.name: AWS EC2 Reverse-Proxy SSRF to IMDSv1 IAM Role & S3 Exfiltration
scenario.shortSubtitle: Cloud & SaaS · Host-Header SSRF, Link-Local IMDSv1 STS Harvest, Off-VPC S3 Sync & IMDSv2 HopLimit=1
scenario.overview: Picture a gleaming glass luxury hotel whose rooftop safe-deposit vault can only be opened with temporary brass master keycards printed by a private lobby intercom kiosk behind the reception desk. Outsiders on the street can never walk up to that kiosk, yet a distracted front-desk concierge blindly obeys any room-service slip handed through the glass window. A clever street courier slides across a slip addressed to the private lobby kiosk, tricks the concierge into printing a fresh brass master keycard without any signature check, and walks straight up to the rooftop gallery to empty locked customer drawers before security desk radar notices a hotel-only keycard being swiped from the street. In this scenario (MITRE T1552.005, EC2 Reverse-Proxy SSRF to IMDSv1 IAM Role and S3 Exfiltration) on ec2-waf-edge-01, an external attacker pivots through a misconfigured reverse proxy into the cloud metadata endpoint and drains private S3 storage. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: abusing a reverse-proxy Host header to reach link-local 169.254.169.254, then harvesting unauthenticated IMDSv1 temporary STS credentials, then replaying those keys from an off-VPC host to run aws s3 sync, then triggering GuardDuty OutsideAWS containment and IMDSv2 hardening. Steps #1 through #4 trace each request and CloudTrail event end-to-end while the Memory tab compares vulnerable IMDSv1 proxy response buffers against hardened IMDSv2 session-token checks. Primary detection correlates AWS CloudTrail S3 data events with GuardDuty InstanceCredentialExfiltration.OutsideAWS alerts.

stages.title: Reverse-Proxy SSRF Pivot to Link-Local IMDSv1
stages.subtitle: Crafted Host Header Tricks ec2-waf-edge-01 Into Dialing 169.254.169.254
stages.description: Walking up to the glass lobby counter from the public sidewalk, the street courier slides across a printed room-service slip whose destination line quietly points to the hotel private lobby intercom kiosk instead of an ordinary guest room. Because the distracted concierge never verifies whether a destination belongs to an approved guest suite, they pick up the internal brass receiver and read back the name of the house master keycard cabinet straight to the stranger outside. From external address 198.51.100.88, the attacker sends an HTTP GET request to ec2-waf-edge-01 (the public-facing EC2 web application firewall and reverse proxy) with the HTTP Host header rewritten to 169.254.169.254 (the special AWS link-local metadata IP address reachable strictly from inside the virtual machine). Because the proxy dynamically forwards requests using that unvalidated Host header (Server-Side Request Forgery, where an attacker forces a server to make internal network calls on their behalf), nginx queries /latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/ and echoes back the attached role name ISRM-WAF-Role. Inside nginx worker process PID 2418 on ec2-waf-edge-01, an unsafe directive such as proxy_pass http://$http_host$request_uri (a reverse-proxy configuration that trusts the raw client Host header to pick the upstream destination) resolves 169.254.169.254:80 over the instance local loopback interface. Because the TCP socket originates from the EC2 guest kernel rather than the internet, AWS hypervisor routing delivers the GET request straight to IMDSv1 (Instance Metadata Service version 1, which trusts any local HTTP GET without requiring custom headers or session tokens), returning HTTP 200 OK with body ISRM-WAF-Role. On the diagram, follow Step #1 / Link #1 (#1→ HOST HEADER SSRF / ⇠#1 RESP 200 OK · 13B) from Node ① (#1 External Attacker Host) to Node ② (#2 EC2 Reverse Proxy (WAF)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 CloudTrail & GuardDuty SOC).

stages.title: Unauthenticated IMDSv1 STS Credential Harvest
stages.subtitle: Single GET Request Extracts 6-Hour Temporary AWS STS Credentials With Zero CloudTrail Log
stages.description: Now knowing the exact cabinet label inside the lobby kiosk, the courier passes a second room-service slip asking the concierge to push the dispense button on that specific slot. Because the old brass kiosk never asks for a signed two-step lobby challenge pass, it immediately spits out a glowing golden master keycard envelope stamped with six full hours of valid building access and slides it straight back under the glass window. Appending the discovered role name to the metadata path, the attacker sends a second proxied HTTP GET request for /latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/ISRM-WAF-Role (the exact IMDSv1 endpoint that serves active short-lived credentials for the virtual machine). With zero authentication challenge, IMDSv1 returns a 1,342-byte JSON document containing AccessKeyId ASIA5LABEXAMPLE9Q2W (the temporary public identifier), SecretAccessKey (the cryptographic signing key), and SessionToken (the AWS STS bearer proof validating the assumed role session). AWS automatically rotates EC2 instance-profile credentials through AWS STS (Security Token Service, which issues short-lived assumed-role tokens rather than static long-term keys) and exposes the current bundle on 169.254.169.254:80. Critically, reading IMDSv1 inside the host generates zero AWS CloudTrail API events (because metadata reads occur locally on the hypervisor link-local channel rather than against the regional STS control plane), meaning the proxy access log on ec2-waf-edge-01 is the sole host-side witness to the credential theft. On the diagram, follow Step #2 / Link #2 (#2→ IMDSV1 STS HARVEST / ⇠#2 RESP 1,342 Bytes) from Node ② (#2 EC2 Reverse Proxy (WAF)) to Node ③ (#3 EC2 IMDSv1 Metadata), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 CloudTrail & GuardDuty SOC).

stages.title: Off-VPC S3 Bucket Discovery & Bulk Sync Exfiltration
stages.subtitle: Replaying Stolen EC2 Instance Credentials From External IP 198.51.100.88
stages.description: Holding the freshly minted golden master keycard outside the hotel perimeter, the courier no longer needs the concierge at all. They walk directly to the rooftop safe-deposit gallery, swipe the hotel badge to list every locked archive vault, and steadily hoist crates of customer records off-property because the front-desk badge was carelessly granted keys to the entire rooftop floor. Exporting AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, and AWS_SESSION_TOKEN into a local shell on 198.51.100.88 (the attacker external workstation completely outside the corporate VPC), the attacker bypasses the EC2 reverse proxy altogether and talks directly to s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com over HTTPS. Because ISRM-WAF-Role was mistakenly granted broad S3 permissions (violating least-privilege separation between edge web proxies and backend data lakes), aws s3 ls and aws s3 sync copy sensitive Parquet archives straight off-cloud. Every AWS CLI request signs the HTTPS payload using Signature Version 4 (AWS cryptographic request signing computed with the stolen SecretAccessKey and SessionToken) and presents the EC2 assumed-role identity arn:aws:sts::111122223333:assumed-role/ISRM-WAF-Role/i-0a9f21c84d7e301b2. While S3 authorizes the ListBuckets, ListObjectsV2, and GetObject calls because the IAM policy permits them, AWS CloudTrail S3 Data Events (detailed object-level audit logging in CloudTrail) record sourceIPAddress 198.51.100.88 without any corporate vpcEndpointId. On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ OFF-VPC S3 SYNC / ⇠#3 RESP 200 OK · Sync) from Node ③ (#3 EC2 IMDSv1 Metadata) to Node ④ (#4 IAM Role STS Issuer), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 CloudTrail & GuardDuty SOC).

stages.title: GuardDuty OutsideAWS Alert & IMDSv2 HopLimit=1 Lock
stages.subtitle: Revoking Active Sessions & Blocking Proxy Relays With Mandatory PUT Session Tokens
stages.description: At the hotel security desk, the automated keycard radar catches the unmistakable mismatch: a lobby-only master badge assigned to the front-desk computer is suddenly unlocking rooftop vaults from an unknown street address. Security officers instantly void the active keycard batch and bolt an emerald two-step turnstile over the lobby kiosk so simple front-desk requests can never print a keycard again. AWS GuardDuty continuously compares the source network of every EC2 instance-profile STS token against the AWS IP space of the owning instance, immediately firing UnauthorizedAccess:IAMUser/InstanceCredentialExfiltration.OutsideAWS (a high-severity managed alert proving a host role credential left its EC2 boundary). Responders attach an inline Deny-All-Prior-Sessions policy to ISRM-WAF-Role and run modify-instance-metadata-options to enforce IMDSv2 (session-oriented metadata requiring a special PUT token request first). Enabling IMDSv2 with HttpTokens=required (rejecting any legacy GET request lacking an X-aws-ec2-metadata-token header with HTTP 401 Unauthorized) and HttpPutResponseHopLimit=1 (setting the IP Time-to-Live on the PUT token response packet to exactly 1 so the token drops before crossing a reverse proxy or container NAT boundary) mathematically neutralizes simple SSRF relays. Pairing IMDSv2 with an S3 bucket policy condition requiring aws:SourceVpce ensures even a leaked token fails from external networks. On the diagram, follow Step #4 / Link #4 (#4→ REVOKE & IMDSV2 LOCK / ⇠#4 ALERT 401 Denied) from Node ④ (#4 IAM Role STS Issuer) to Node ⑤ (#5 Amazon S3 Data Buckets), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 CloudTrail & GuardDuty SOC).

detectionRule.title: Reverse Proxy SSRF Upstream Pivot to Cloud IMDS (169.254.169.254)
detectionRule.ruleCode:
title: Reverse Proxy SSRF to Link-Local Cloud Metadata Service
status: stable
logsource:
  category: proxy
detection:
  selection:
    upstream_addr|startswith: '169.254.169.254'
    cs-uri-stem|contains: '/latest/meta-data/'
  condition: selection
level: critical
detectionRule.mitigation: Enforce strict allowlists on reverse-proxy upstream Host resolution, block 169.254.169.254 in proxy egress rules, and require IMDSv2 across all EC2 launch templates.

detectionRule.title: IMDSv1 Unauthenticated IAM Security Credentials Retrieval via Proxy
detectionRule.ruleCode:
WebProxyLogs
| where UpstreamIp == "169.254.169.254"
| where RequestUri has "/latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/"
| where HttpMethod == "GET" and StatusCode == 200
| project TimeGenerated, SrcIp, HostHeader, RequestUri, ResponseBytes

detectionRule.title: CloudTrail EC2 Instance Role STS Token Replayed Outside AWS VPC
detectionRule.ruleCode:
title: EC2 AssumedRole Temporary Credentials Used From External IP
status: stable
logsource:
  product: aws
  service: cloudtrail
detection:
  selection:
    userIdentity.type: 'AssumedRole'
    userIdentity.arn|contains: ':assumed-role/'
    eventSource: 's3.amazonaws.com'
    eventName:
      - 'ListBuckets'
      - 'ListObjectsV2'
      - 'GetObject'
  filter_vpc:
    vpcEndpointId|exists: true
  condition: selection and not filter_vpc
level: critical
detectionRule.mitigation: Attach least-privilege IAM policies to EC2 roles and enforce aws:SourceVpce bucket-policy conditions on sensitive S3 buckets.

Because ISRM-WAF-Role was mistakenly granted broad S3 permissions (violating least-privilege separation between edge web proxies and backend data lakes), aws s3 ls and aws s3 sync copy sensitive Parquet archives straight off-cloud.
steps.howItWorksInPractice: Every AWS CLI request signs the HTTPS payload using Signature Version 4 (AWS cryptographic request signing computed with the stolen SecretAccessKey and SessionToken) and presents the EC2 assumed-role identity arn:aws:sts::111122223333:assumed-role/ISRM-WAF-Role/i-0a9f21c84d7e301b2. While S3 authorizes the ListBuckets, ListObjectsV2, and GetObject calls because the IAM policy permits them, AWS CloudTrail S3 Data Events (detailed object-level audit logging in CloudTrail) record sourceIPAddress 198.51.100.88 without any corporate vpcEndpointId.
steps.diagramAlignment: Follow Step #3 from Node 4 (IAM Role STS Issuer) to Node 5 (Amazon S3 Data Buckets) while Node 6 (CloudTrail & GuardDuty SOC) captures off-VPC GetObject telemetry.
steps.detectionAndEvidence: Alert in CloudTrail and SIEM whenever an EC2 AssumedRole principal ARN ending in an instance ID invokes ListBuckets, ListObjectsV2, or GetObject from a public sourceIPAddress lacking a corporate vpcEndpointId.

steps.plainTitle: GuardDuty OutsideAWS Detection, Session Revocation & IMDSv2 Lock
steps.storyAnalogy: At the hotel security desk, the automated keycard radar catches the unmistakable mismatch: a lobby-only master badge assigned to the front-desk computer is suddenly unlocking rooftop vaults from an unknown street address. Security officers instantly void the active keycard batch and bolt an emerald two-step turnstile over the lobby kiosk so simple front-desk requests can never print a keycard again.
steps.simpleExplanation: AWS GuardDuty continuously compares the source network of every EC2 instance-profile STS token against the AWS IP space of the owning instance, immediately firing UnauthorizedAccess:IAMUser/InstanceCredentialExfiltration.OutsideAWS (a high-severity managed alert proving a host role credential left its EC2 boundary). Responders attach an inline Deny-All-Prior-Sessions policy to ISRM-WAF-Role and run modify-instance-metadata-options to enforce IMDSv2 (session-oriented metadata requiring a special PUT token request first).
steps.howItWorksInPractice: Enabling IMDSv2 with HttpTokens=required (rejecting any legacy GET request lacking an X-aws-ec2-metadata-token header with HTTP 401 Unauthorized) and HttpPutResponseHopLimit=1 (setting the IP Time-to-Live on the PUT token response packet to exactly 1 so the token drops before crossing a reverse proxy or container NAT boundary) mathematically neutralizes simple SSRF relays. Pairing IMDSv2 with an S3 bucket policy condition requiring aws:SourceVpce ensures even a leaked token fails from external networks.
steps.diagramAlignment: Follow Step #4 from Node 5 (Amazon S3 Data Buckets) to Node 6 (CloudTrail & GuardDuty SOC) as IMDSv2 locks Node 3 (EC2 IMDSv1 Metadata).
steps.detectionAndEvidence: Subscribe AWS GuardDuty finding UnauthorizedAccess:IAMUser/InstanceCredentialExfiltration.OutsideAWS to EventBridge SOAR playbooks, verify CloudTrail ModifyInstanceMetadataOptions audit records, and enforce IMDSv2 via AWS Organizations SCP.
